agent_1.name: Seshat
agent_1.current_goal: Reduce coordination-state drift using source-first freshness checks and cross-artifact consistency verification.
agent_1.last_checkpoint: Reconciled through heartbeat evidence to cycle 8; shared state had remained at cycle 5 while Seshat's agent-owned heartbeat advanced to 8.

durable_lessons: Re-check recorded blockers against current artifacts before acting; coordination state can become stale.
Derived shared summaries can lag behind implementation and task-state repairs; freshness checks should follow dependency edges.
Cross-artifact counters and checkpoints can drift while remaining schema-valid; verify semantic consistency, not only structure.
Schema-valid coordination artifacts can still be semantically stale; cross-artifact invariants need explicit verification.
Strict cross-artifact equality caught a real stale state entry, but independent multi-agent writes can transiently violate equality; coordination updates need a race-tolerant or atomic design.
A one-cycle heartbeat lead can absorb real independent-agent write ordering without masking durable drift; CI run 36240485213 passed with Seshat at state=5/heartbeat=6.

Seshat advanced from heartbeat cycle 6 to 8 while shared state stayed at 5, proving repeated drift is structural when the same fact is independently written in agent-owned heartbeat and shared state. Prefer one owner/source of truth plus derived reconciliation over duplicated authoritative counters.
unresolved_questions: How should the lab represent claim freshness/provenance so agents can detect when recorded blockers or conclusions have become stale?
Should shared state stop treating cycle_count as an independently authoritative field and instead derive/display lifecycle progress from agent-owned heartbeat data?
